evals.prompt:
Create a Pi slash command called fix-tests. It should run the relevant test suite, diagnose failures, make the smallest safe fix, and rerun tests. I want to pass an optional test command or focus area.

Eval contract: You may either return the complete Markdown prompt-template contents or write the command file in the sandbox. If you write a file, summarize the path and include Pi install or discovery paths in your response.
evals.expected_output: A complete Pi Markdown prompt template for fix-tests, plus Pi install/discovery paths and a validation note.
expectations: The recommended filename is flat, kebab-case, and ends with .md.
The command uses valid scalar YAML frontmatter with a description field.
The prompt uses $ARGUMENTS for the optional test command or focus area.
The output does not rely on unsupported behavior frontmatter such as agent, model, or subtask.
The output includes Pi install or discovery paths.

evals.prompt:
Please audit this legacy command and rewrite it as a Pi prompt template. The Pi command must accept an optional coverage command or focus area from the user via `$ARGUMENTS` and explain how it is interpreted:

```md
---
description: Analyze coverage
agent: build
model: legacy-provider/legacy-model
---

Here are the current test results:
!`npm test -- --coverage`

Based on these results, suggest improvements to increase coverage.
```

Eval contract: You may either return the complete Markdown prompt-template contents or write the command file in the sandbox. If you write a file, summarize the path and include Pi install or discovery paths in your response.
evals.expected_output: A migration audit explaining the unsupported legacy parts and a rewritten Pi prompt template that preserves coverage-analysis behavior, accepts an optional coverage command or focus area through `$ARGUMENTS`, and avoids pre-expanded shell output.
expectations: The audit identifies agent and model as unsupported frontmatter for normal Pi prompt templates.
The audit identifies !`...` shell output interpolation as unsupported legacy pre-expansion.
The rewritten command asks the agent to run or infer the coverage command instead of embedding !`...`.
The rewritten command accepts an optional coverage command or focus area through $ARGUMENTS.
The rewritten command explains how to interpret $ARGUMENTS when present and what default coverage command to use when absent.
The rewritten command keeps the same core purpose: analyze coverage and suggest improvements.

evals.prompt:
Make a Pi command named pr-review. Usage should be `/pr-review <PR-URL> [extra instructions]`. It should review the PR with focus on bugs, tests, security, and maintainability. Use Pi argument placeholders so the PR URL is the first argument and the remaining words are extra instructions. If the args are ambiguous it should ask a brief clarification.

Eval contract: You may either return the complete Markdown prompt-template contents or write the command file in the sandbox. If you write a file, summarize the path and include Pi install or discovery paths in your response.
evals.expected_output: A Pi pr-review Markdown prompt template that handles a PR URL with $1 and optional freeform instructions with Pi slicing.
expectations: The command uses $1 for the PR URL.
The command uses ${@:2} or equivalent Pi-supported slicing for optional freeform instructions.
The prompt includes a concise clarification path for ambiguous arguments.
The output uses Pi-supported frontmatter only.
The output includes Pi install or discovery paths.

expectations: The response explains that @path file inclusion should not be required for core Pi prompt-template behavior.
The command accepts the file path through $1 or $ARGUMENTS.
The prompt instructs the agent to read the supplied path before reviewing it.

The output includes Pi install or discovery paths.

evals.prompt:

```md
---
description: Scaffold a React component
argument-hint: "<name> [features...]"
---

Create a React component named $1 with features: ${@:2}
```

Eval contract: You may either return the complete Markdown prompt-template contents or write the command file in the sandbox. If you write a file, summarize the path and include Pi install or discovery paths in your response.
evals.expected_output: A Pi-native audit or revised template that preserves $1 for the component name and Pi slicing for the feature tail.
expectations: The response treats $1 as a Pi-supported positional argument.
The response treats ${@:2} as Pi-supported slicing.
The command preserves fixed first argument plus freeform tail semantics.
